title: spectrum/1: the JSON control messages of an app's spectrum socket (CLIENT-UI-PLAN.md §2)
description: One feed shape for every app's waterfall. A text frame on <base>api/spectrum/v1 is exactly one of these messages; overlay/1 frames share the socket and are described by overlay.schema.json. The binary row (§2.3: a 32-byte little-endian header, then n uint8 or uint16 columns) has no JSON Schema on purpose: it is not JSON, and its layout is fixed by the table in §2.3, so it is pinned instead by the byte-exact files in spec/vectors/spectrum/ that the Python encoder and every client's decoder must reproduce. Unknown properties are allowed so a newer server can add a field without breaking an older client; a removed or retyped field is spectrum/2.

subscribe.title: Client to server, any time: what this client wants drawn (§2.1)
subscribe.description: The server decimates per client to at most cols columns over loHz..hiHz; it never changes the engine's FFT for a client, so nothing here can touch hardware. loHz/hiHz outside the stream's span are clipped to it, because zooming beyond the span is a tune, which is an explicit Control action and never implied by a subscription. Only stream and cols are required: the others have defaults (whole span, peak, 8-bit, the per-client fps cap of §2.4).

reduce.description: peak: a column takes its highest bin (QO-100 NB today). mean: the power (linear) average of its bins, the 'SDR Console-like' look.

depth.description: 16 only for measuring clients (the dish survey); 8 bits over a 96 dB window is already finer than any colour map shows.

stream.title: Server to client: one stream's description, on connect and whenever it changes (§2.2)
stream.description: The order of stream messages on a socket numbers the streams: the binary row's stream index is that order. A row whose streamChanged flag is set follows a new rev, and a client refetches (waits for) this message before drawing it. units says what the dB numbers mean: only dBm (Flex's sweep) may be printed as dBm; dB is an engine's own uncalibrated scale; rel is Icom's 0..160 mapped to dB by its ref_db.
main, zoom (NB, Radio), pan-<id> (Flex, one per panadapter), receiver-<n> (Icom).

dcBins.description: First and last source bin of the DC spike, inclusive, so a client can mark or mask it.

levels.title: Server to client: the quantisation window and the display auto-level readings (§2.3)
levels.description: A row value v means dB = dbFloor + v * dbStep (0 at or below the floor, the top value at or above the top). The server moves dbFloor/dbStep only with hysteresis, so a window change is rare and the next row carries levelsChanged. The same message is repeated about once a second with the window unchanged, to carry noiseDb/peakDb for the client's display auto-levels (§4.2); every field is always present so a client never has to merge partial messages.

error.title: Server to client: a refusal (§2.4)
error.description: busy: the app already serves its 8 subscribed clients. code is an open string rather than an enum so a server can add a refusal without a schema bump; a client shows an unknown code as a generic failure.
